Using the root-of-unity filter with \(\omega = e^{2\pi i / 502}\), we have
\[
S_r = \frac{1}{502} \sum_{j=0}^{501} \omega^{-jr} (1 + \omega^j)^{10000}.
\]

Also, since \(\omega\) is a primitive \(502\)th root of unity in \(\mathbb{F}_{503}\) (as \(502 \mid 503-1\)), we have \((1 + \omega^j)^{502} = 1\) for \(1 + \omega^j \ne 0\). The only case where \(1 + \omega^j = 0\) is when \(j = 251\), giving \((1 + \omega^{251})^{10000} = 0\). For other \(j\), reducing the exponent modulo \(502\) gives
\[
(1 + \omega^j)^{10000} = (1 + \omega^j)^{462}.
\]
Thus,
\[
S_r \equiv -\sum_{j=0}^{501} \omega^{-jr} (1 + \omega^j)^{462} \pmod{503}.
\]
By the inverse discrete Fourier transform,
\[
\sum_{j=0}^{501} \omega^{-jr} (1 + \omega^j)^{462} = 502 \sum_{m \ge 0} \binom{462}{502m + r}.
\]
Therefore,
\[
S_r \equiv -\left(502 \sum_{m \ge 0} \binom{462}{502m + r}\right) \equiv \sum_{m \ge 0} \binom{462}{502m + r} \pmod{503}.
\]
Let \(T_r = \sum_{m \ge 0} \binom{462}{502m + r}\). Since \(0 \le r \le 501\) and \(462 < 502\), we have:
- For \(0 \le r \le 462\), the only possible term is when \(502m + r = r\) (i.e., \(m = 0\)), so \(T_r = \binom{462}{r}\).
- For \(463 \le r \le 501\), there is no integer \(m\) such that \(0 \le 502m + r \le 462\), so \(T_r = 0\).

Hence,
\[
S_r \equiv 
\begin{cases}
\binom{462}{r} \pmod{503}, & 0 \le r \le 462, \\
0 \pmod{503}, & 463 \le r \le 501.
\end{cases}
\]

Since \(503 > 462\), the prime \(503\) does not divide any factor in \(\binom{462}{r}\) for \(0 \le r \le 462\), so \(\binom{462}{r} \not\equiv 0 \pmod{503}\). Thus, \(S_r\) is a multiple of \(503\) if and only if \(463 \le r \le 501\).

The number of such \(r\) is \(501 - 463 + 1 = 39\).
